title: SignBridge
summary: A two-way sign-language communication experience that translates hand gestures into readable text and helps hearing users respond with visual signing guidance.
problem: Communication barriers grow when sign-language users and hearing users do not share a fluent language. The interaction needed to support both sides of a conversation instead of offering a one-direction classifier demo.
system: The application observes hand gestures through a camera, translates supported signs into readable text, and provides a visual response path so the hearing participant can communicate back without pretending to replace a human interpreter.

engineeringDecisions.title: Design for a two-way exchange
engineeringDecisions.detail: Recognition and response guidance live in one conversational flow rather than as disconnected demonstrations.

engineeringDecisions.title: Keep camera feedback visible
engineeringDecisions.detail: Users can see the live input and recognition state while forming a gesture.

reliability.title: Explicit supported vocabulary
reliability.detail: The interface communicates the supported alphabet and space gesture rather than implying unrestricted sign-language translation.

reliability.title: Confidence-aware recognition
reliability.detail: Recognition feedback helps distinguish a detected gesture from an uncertain frame.

result: An accessibility-focused computer-vision product that frames gesture recognition as part of a usable two-way conversation.

evidence.label: Source repository
evidence.description: Computer-vision models and the interactive communication application.

title: RelayDesk
summary: A real-time voice support agent that resolves payment questions through a constrained tool surface, explicit escalation rules, and session-level safety limits.
problem: A payment support voice agent must be fast enough for conversation while remaining predictable around sensitive account actions, unsupported requests, escalation, and session cost.
system: A web client opens a LiveKit voice session, while a server-side agent interprets the request and uses a narrow MCP toolset for approved payment-support actions. The experience confirms outcomes, escalates unresolved cases, and ends within a defined session limit.

engineeringDecisions.title: Constrain the operational surface
engineeringDecisions.detail: The agent can act only through seven purpose-built support tools instead of broad account or database access.

engineeringDecisions.title: Make escalation a product path
engineeringDecisions.detail: Unsupported or unresolved requests lead to an explicit handoff rather than a confident invented answer.

engineeringDecisions.title: Bound every session
engineeringDecisions.detail: A five-minute session ceiling keeps the demo, latency, and provider usage predictable.

reliability.title: Scenario-based evaluation
reliability.detail: Fifteen expected support scenarios exercise common resolutions, failure handling, and escalation behavior.

reliability.title: Server-side credentials
reliability.detail: Provider and tool credentials remain outside the browser-facing application.

reliability.title: Outcome confirmation
reliability.detail: The agent restates consequential results so the caller can catch misunderstandings before ending the session.

result: A deployable voice-support experience that combines conversational speed with a deliberately narrow action boundary and tested escalation behavior.

evidence.label: Source repository
evidence.description: Voice agent, support tools, evaluation scenarios, and web experience.
